set.st: Harris Schultz, aged 62 (an earlier OCR read "12") lived alone in Springbrook [Spencer Brook] township near Cambridge and was found dead in September 1914. He was afraid to keep his money in banks, and it was supposed that several thousand dollars were buried somewhere near his home. His only known relative was a sister in Minneapolis, and a search was to be made. "Springbrook" in the Cambridge wire story is a garble of Spencer Brook Twp beside Cambridge (Kanabec Co has no such township); no follow-up found through 1917. Pin is approximate (town or township only), not the spot itself. LiDAR cache check (USGS 1 m, 2022): LiDAR shows a cellar-sized pit, about 21 x 14 m and 0.9 m deep 1081 m southeast of the pin (45.50732, -93.44124), worth a look: fits a house cellar near his home; the pin is only to the township. Records check: Princeton Union, Sept. 24, 1914: Harris Schultz was found dead in his home 'at the old Emerson farm in Spencer Brook', where he lived alone; neighbors noticed his stock neglected. An Emerson name on a Spencer Brook Twp. plat or patent would place the farm.
